subject: economics
title: Wages & Salaries Adventure
welcome_lead: How do people get paid? Let's find out. 💸
meta_desc: Jobs & Earnings Adventure 2 — KS3 Economics on wages, salaries, bonuses and pay.
final_note: You learned the difference between wages and salaries, plus bonuses and overtime.

concepts.def: Pay based on what you sell

walkthroughs.body_html:
A wage is paid per hour worked.

A salary is fixed yearly, split into monthly payments.

Wages are common for shop and trade work. Salaries for office work.

Many earn extras:

  • Bonus — reward for good work.
  • Overtime — extra hours, often time-and-a-half.
  • Commission — % of what you sell, common in car sales.

Gross pay = before tax. Net pay = after tax.

£30,000 salary → roughly £24,000 net after tax & NI. 💷

Tax goes to the government, NI to NHS and pensions.

mcqs.q: What determines the size of the fiscal multiplier?
options: Mainly the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) — the higher the share of extra income people spend domestically, the bigger the multiplier. Leakages (saving, imports, taxes) reduce the multiplier.
The fiscal multiplier is always 2 or 3.
